To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the combination of directional compliant joint and active tail enables various transitions for a climbing robot.
a modular climbing robot with directional compliant joints and an active tail is able to achieve various internal and external transition passively.
a novel under-actuated climbing robot with a passive compliant joint and active tail is proposed to achieve various internal and external transitioning capabilities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a new type of modular under-actuated climbing robot that can perform various types of internal and external transitions.
developing a new type of under-actuated climbing robot with various transition abilities.
the design and development of an underactuated tank-like robot with compliant joints and an active tail to enable various internal/external transitions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed robot is a novel and efficient solution to the problem of internal and external transitions in climbing robots, and that this research has made significant contributions in this field.
the robot presented in this paper has a unique design which enables various transitions and is driven by a tread-wheel mechanism to realize fast and stable climbing.
the presented climbing robot has the potential to perform various internal transitions, external transitions and thin-wall transitions passively and robustly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the robot can climb on vertical walls, climb on ceilings, and transition from a vertical surface to a horizontal surface and vice versa, all without any external assistance.
we developed a novel climbing robot that can perform various internal and transitions without complex control.
we present an innovative under-actuated tank robot that can climb on vertical walls with various transitions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple under-actuated robot can perform various transitions with a simple control.
the robot can be controlled passively by using the directional compliance and the active tail.
under-actuated systems can be used for complex tasks such as climbing and transitioning.
